# Objects and Classes

A **class** is a type you write. An **instance** is an object of that type. Methods are functions that receive the instance (`self`).

## Planned chapters

| Chapter | Focus |
|---------|--------|
| `class` and `self` | Instances, `__init__` |
| Dunder basics | `__repr__`, `__eq__`, `__len__` |
| Inheritance and `super` | When to compose instead |
| Dataclasses | Records without boilerplate |
| Protocols / ABC | “Looks like” vs “is a” (with Typing) |

Until these leaves exist: official [Classes](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/classes.html) tutorial, then Internals → [Object model](../14-internals/01-object-model.qmd) and [Descriptors](../14-internals/07-descriptors-and-slots.qmd).

Ramalho’s *Fluent Python* is the deep track for the data model.
